```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("VWARP_VIGNETTES"), "true")
)
```

Sentinel-2 tiles come in the UTM zone they fall in, so an area that crosses
a zone boundary arrives in two coordinate systems. Meridian 144 degrees
east, the line between zones 54 and 55, runs through the Great Ocean Road
in Victoria, Australia. This vignette takes the two tiles from one overpass
(3 February 2026), tile 54HYC in zone 54 and 55HBT in zone 55, and warps
three bands of each, as floating-point surface reflectance, onto one grid:
GDA94 / Australian Albers (EPSG:3577) at 100 m.

The usual way to do this is to give gdalwarp both tiles as inputs, through
`gdalraster::warp()`, `terra::project()` on a mosaic, or `gdalwarp` itself.
Here each tile is planned and warped with rwarp, the two results are
combined the way gdalwarp combines its inputs, and the end compares that
with gdalwarp's own mosaic of the same sources.

The vignette reads from the network (Element 84's Earth Search catalogue of
Sentinel-2 on AWS), so its code runs only with `VWARP_VIGNETTES=true`.

```{r libraries}
library(rwarp)
library(gdalraster)
```

## The two tiles

Each band of a Sentinel-2 L2A tile is its own cloud-optimised GeoTIFF:
16-bit integers with 0 for nodata, which become reflectance as
`dn * 0.0001 - 0.1`. The item paths below came from a search of Earth
Search's STAC API (collection `sentinel-2-c1-l2a`) at 144 E, 38.3 S.

The destination is 100 m, so we read an overview of each band rather than
its 10 m pixels: `vrt://...?ovr=2` opens the third overview (about 80 m) as
an ordinary raster. gdalwarp picks an overview by itself when it
downsamples (`-ovr AUTO`); rwarp warps whatever `read_fn` reads, so the
choice is made here, in the source path.

```{r sources}
base <- paste0("/vsicurl/https://e84-earth-search-sentinel-data.s3.",
               "us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sentinel-2-c1-l2a")
scenes <- c(
  "54HYC" = "54/H/YC/2026/2/S2C_T54HYC_20260203T002054_L2A",
  "55HBT" = "55/H/BT/2026/2/S2C_T55HBT_20260203T002054_L2A"
)
bands <- c(red = "B04", green = "B03", blue = "B02")
src_path <- function(scene, band) {
  sprintf("vrt://%s/%s/%s.tif?ovr=2", base, scene, band)
}

src <- lapply(scenes, function(s) {
  lapply(bands, function(b) new(GDALRaster, src_path(s, b)))
})
info <- lapply(src, function(ds) list(
  crs = ds$red$getProjectionRef(),
  gt  = ds$red$getGeoTransform(),
  dim = as.integer(c(ds$red$getRasterXSize(), ds$red$getRasterYSize()))
))

t(sapply(info, function(i) c(crs = srs_get_name(i$crs),
                             pixel = round(i$gt[2], 2),
                             size = paste(i$dim, collapse = " x "))))
```

## One destination grid

A longitude/latitude box across the zone boundary, taken into Albers and
snapped to 100 m:

```{r destination}
dst_crs <- "EPSG:3577"
res     <- 100
ll  <- c(143.3, 144.8, -38.9, -38.05)   # xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax
ext <- reproj::reproj_extent(ll, dst_crs, source = "EPSG:4326")
ext <- c(floor(ext[1] / res), ceiling(ext[2] / res),
         floor(ext[3] / res), ceiling(ext[4] / res)) * res
dst_dim <- as.integer(round(c(ext[2] - ext[1], ext[4] - ext[3]) / res))
dst_gt  <- c(ext[1], res, 0, ext[4], 0, -res)
dst_dim
```

## A plan for each tile

Each tile is a different source in a different CRS, so each gets its own
plan against the same destination. No pixels are read yet.

The plans are made as gdalwarp makes its own, so that the comparison at the
end holds pixel for pixel. That means describing the warp as gdalwarp will
see it, three bands worked as Float64 with nodata, and using gdalwarp's
rules for splitting and for the kernel scale (see "Planning as gdalwarp
does" in `?warp_plan`).

```{r plan}
alg <- "cubic"
plans <- lapply(info, function(i) {
  warp_plan(i$crs, i$gt, i$dim, dst_crs, dst_gt,
            dst_size = dst_dim, resample = alg,
            nbands = length(bands), working_type = "Float64", src_nodata = 0,
            min_fill_ratio = 0.5, min_dst_size = 100L, scale_origin = "output")
})
do.call(rbind, lapply(names(plans), function(s) {
  ch <- unlist(plans[[s]], recursive = FALSE)
  cbind(tile = s, do.call(rbind, lapply(ch, as.data.frame)))
}))
```

Three Float64 bands and their nodata masks take 195 bits a pixel, and this
destination with a tile's source doesn't fit gdalwarp's default 64 MB of
working memory in one piece, so each plan splits it into a left and a right
half. Each half reads only the part of the tile it needs. `fill_ratio` is
the share of the source area a chunk maps onto that the tile actually has,
lowest for the left half of 55HBT's plan, much of which lies beyond the
tile's west edge, in zone 54. `scale_x` and `scale_y` are near 0.8, the 80 m overview going
to 100 m: the cubic kernel widens to match, as gdalwarp's does when it
downsamples, and each chunk estimates its own.

With `warp_plan()`'s defaults the plan would be one chunk per tile, with
one estimate of the kernel scale for the whole destination. That reads the
same pixels, but it isn't how gdalwarp would warp this, and for some kernels
and sizes the values differ from gdalwarp's (by up to 1 DN with lanczos
here, and by up to 93 DN with cubic at 50 m).

## Reading three bands as reflectance

`read_fn` returns every band of the window in one vector, each band
row-major, one after another. Here it also turns the integers into
reflectance, with NaN for nodata, so the warp works on doubles.

```{r read-fn}
reader <- function(ds) {
  function(xoff, yoff, xsize, ysize) {
    dn <- unlist(lapply(ds, function(d) d$read(1L, xoff, yoff, xsize, ysize,
                                               xsize, ysize)))
    refl <- dn * 1e-4 - 0.1
    refl[dn == 0] <- NaN
    refl
  }
}
```

## Warp each tile, then combine

```{r warp}
warped <- lapply(names(scenes), function(s) {
  i <- info[[s]]
  warp_exec(plans[[s]], reader(src[[s]]), i$crs, i$gt, dst_crs, dst_gt,
            nbands = length(bands))
})
names(warped) <- names(scenes)
str(warped[["54HYC"]])
```

Each result is an array `c(nrow, ncol, 3)` of reflectance, `NaN` where the
tile doesn't reach (`is.na()` is `TRUE` there). gdalwarp, given several inputs, warps them in order and
each one writes over the destination wherever it has a value. The same here:

```{r mosaic}
mosaic <- warped[["54HYC"]]
later  <- !is.na(warped[["55HBT"]])
mosaic[later] <- warped[["55HBT"]][later]
c(`54HYC` = mean(!is.na(warped[["54HYC"]])),
  `55HBT` = mean(!is.na(warped[["55HBT"]])),
  mosaic  = mean(!is.na(mosaic)))
```

Each tile sits at its own angle in Albers:

```{r plot-tiles, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 3.4}
stretch <- function(a) {
  a[] <- pmin(1, pmax(0, a / 0.18))^(1 / 1.6)
  a
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
for (s in names(warped)) {
  ximage::ximage(stretch(warped[[s]]), ext, asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
                 main = paste(s, "in EPSG:3577"))
}
par(op)
```

and together they fill the box apart from its corners. The dashed line is
144 E, the boundary between the zones:

```{r plot-mosaic, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 6}
op <- par(mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
ximage::ximage(stretch(mosaic), ext, asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
               main = "54HYC and 55HBT, 3 February 2026")
lines(reproj::reproj_xy(cbind(144, seq(-38.95, -38, by = 0.05)),
                        dst_crs, source = "EPSG:4326"), lty = 2, col = "white")
par(op)
```

## The same with gdalwarp

gdalwarp with both tiles as inputs, from the same overview pixels:
`-ovr NONE` so it doesn't pick another overview, and `-ot Float64` so it
doesn't round to integers. gdalwarp warps the integers and the reflectance
scaling comes after; the kernels are weighted means, so that order gives the
same values up to rounding.

```{r gdalwarp}
vrt <- vapply(scenes, function(s) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".vrt")
  buildVRT(f, vapply(bands, function(b) src_path(s, b), ""),
           cl_arg = "-separate", quiet = TRUE)
  f
}, "")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
warp(unname(vrt), out, t_srs = dst_crs, quiet = TRUE, cl_arg = c(
  "-te", ext[c(1, 3, 2, 4)], "-ts", dst_dim, "-r", alg,
  "-ot", "Float64", "-srcnodata", "0", "-dstnodata", "0",
  "-ovr", "NONE"))

g  <- new(GDALRaster, out)
gd <- array(NA_real_, dim(mosaic))
for (b in seq_along(bands)) {
  dn <- matrix(g$read(b, 0, 0, dst_dim[1], dst_dim[2], dst_dim[1], dst_dim[2]),
               nrow = dst_dim[2], byrow = TRUE)
  gd[, , b] <- ifelse(dn == 0, NA, dn * 1e-4 - 0.1)
}
g$close()

identical(is.na(mosaic), is.na(gd))   # the same pixels have data
max(abs(mosaic - gd), na.rm = TRUE)   # and the same values, to rounding
```

## Warp again without reading again

`warp_exec()` reads through `read_fn` every time it runs. To try other
kernels without reading again, read once and give the pixels to
`warp_buffer()`, which warps one source window into one destination window:
the step `warp_exec()` runs for each chunk. Here that's the window all of
55HBT's chunks need, read once, and each chunk warped from it with its own
kernel scale:

```{r buffer}
chs <- plans[["55HBT"]][[1]]
i   <- info[["55HBT"]]
lo  <- c(min(sapply(chs, `[[`, "src_xoff")), min(sapply(chs, `[[`, "src_yoff")))
hi  <- c(max(sapply(chs, function(ch) ch$src_xoff + ch$src_xsize)),
         max(sapply(chs, function(ch) ch$src_yoff + ch$src_ysize)))
win <- reader(src[["55HBT"]])(lo[1], lo[2], hi[1] - lo[1], hi[2] - lo[2])

again <- function(resample) {
  out <- array(NaN, c(dst_dim[2], dst_dim[1], length(bands)))
  for (ch in chs) {
    rows <- ch$dst_yoff + seq_len(ch$dst_ysize)
    cols <- ch$dst_xoff + seq_len(ch$dst_xsize)
    out[rows, cols, ] <- warp_buffer(
      win, i$crs, i$gt, dst_crs, dst_gt,
      dst_off = c(ch$dst_xoff, ch$dst_yoff), dst_size = c(ch$dst_xsize, ch$dst_ysize),
      src_off = lo, src_size = hi - lo, src_dim = i$dim, resample = resample,
      scaling = "fixed", scale = c(ch$scale_x, ch$scale_y))
  }
  out
}
identical(again("cubic"), warped[["55HBT"]])

## how far nearest neighbour and averaging are from cubic, in reflectance
sapply(c(near = "near", average = "average"), function(r) {
  stats::quantile(abs(again(r) - warped[["55HBT"]]), c(0.5, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
})
```

```{r close, include = FALSE}
for (ds in src) for (d in ds) d$close()
```

## HLS

Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) uses the same tiling and the same UTM
zones, so the same steps apply: a plan per tile, a `read_fn` that scales the
bands (HLS stores reflectance as `dn * 0.0001` with -9999 for nodata), and
the tiles combined in order. HLS is served from NASA's LP DAAC and needs an
Earthdata login for GDAL to read it.
